source_idea: Could a small model learn to rewrite a changing tool graph while agents work, so the team uses less context and fewer expensive model calls?

constraints.time: Two weeks for the first decision
constraints.cash: Prefer less than USD 1,000 excluding labor
constraints.compute: One local GPU or metered APIs

formalizations.title: Offline learned tool-graph router
formalizations.problem: Agents repeatedly expose irrelevant tools and context.
formalizations.mechanism: Train a small router on logged tasks to select and order a task-specific tool subgraph before execution.
formalizations.success_metric: Reduce tool-schema tokens and expensive-model calls without reducing task success.
innovation_delta: Jointly selects tools and dependency order under a cost constraint

innovation.rationale: The combination is plausible, but the bounded novelty scan is not yet complete.

plausibility.rationale: A replay benchmark can test routing without online training.

commercialization.rationale: The buyer and savings metric are clear, but demand is unverified.

resource_fit.rationale: A log-replay prototype fits one developer and a local GPU.

resource_estimate.hardware: One 24 GB GPU or a small metered training job
resource_estimate.data: At least several hundred permissioned tool-use traces

cheapest_test.decision_question: Does learned routing beat retrieval and rules at equal task success?
cheapest_test.minimal_artifact: Offline router plus replay harness over a fixed trace set
cheapest_test.baseline: All tools, rule filter, and embedding retrieval
cheapest_test.metric: Task success, schema tokens, expensive-model calls, and recovery rate
cheapest_test.pass_threshold: At least 25% token reduction and 15% fewer expensive calls with no more than 2 percentage points success loss
cheapest_test.fail_threshold: Less than 10% savings or more than 5 percentage points success loss
cheapest_test.largest_confound: Replay cannot capture all downstream effects of a missing tool
cheapest_test.next_if_pass: Run a shadow-mode online test on one workflow
cheapest_test.next_if_fail: Keep deterministic retrieval and drop learned graph rewriting

formalizations.title: Online self-rewriting multi-agent graph
formalizations.problem: A fixed orchestration graph adapts poorly during long tasks.
formalizations.mechanism: Continuously retrain routing and dependency structure from live rewards while agents execute.
formalizations.success_metric: Improve long-horizon task success per dollar over a fixed orchestrator.
nearest_neighbors: Online reinforcement learning for tool use
innovation_delta: Live structural updates rather than pre-task routing

innovation.rationale: The live structure claim may differ from ordinary routers, but prior art is not exhausted.

plausibility.rationale: Delayed rewards and unsafe exploration make representative validation difficult.

commercialization.rationale: The initial buyer set is narrow and operational risk is high.

resource_fit.rationale: Representative training appears to require large proprietary traces and frontier-scale execution.

fatal_constraints: No faithful low-cost test for live reward and failure dynamics has been identified
Representative data and execution scale are outside the stated envelope

resource_estimate.hardware: Large distributed inference and training fleet
resource_estimate.cash_range: Unknown but incompatible with the stated cap
resource_estimate.data: Large proprietary online agent traces with rewards

next_action: Run the capped offline replay test for F1 before designing any online learner.
unknowns: Permission and volume of available traces
Current prior art on learned dependency-order selection
Actual per-call savings in the target workflow

evidence_register.claim: F1 can be evaluated with a replay harness
One developer and one GPU are sufficient for the first test
evidence_register.source: Assumes existing permissioned traces and a small router
